title: Parallel streams: when they help and when they get in the way

videos.script: One word turns a stream parallel: parallel. This lesson is about when that word is worth writing. {{threads}} First, who does the work. Print the thread name inside the pipeline, and the elements are spread over the main thread and three workers from a shared pool, one per processor. {{fast}} Then the measurement. Counting primes below two million takes a little over a quarter of the time on four processors. {{slow}} Summing a hundred small numbers takes longer in parallel than in a plain loop, because splitting and joining cost more than the work. {{wrong}} And the case that is not slow but wrong: lambdas that change a shared list. The list loses elements, or the program crashes, and which one happens changes from run to run.
